chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Mixed ancestry and doubts about African origins theories
summary: They discuss ethnic mixture in England and America and doubt generalised theories about African origins of jazz.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, you know, the -- it's like I'm supposed to be English, but my mother was Scottish, and my -- on my grandmother's side they were Huguenots from France. My father was born in Wales, although his father was Eng -- but now, in my opinion, you'd have a hell of a job to find a pure blooded Englishman in England. They're all mixed up. I mean there's been Danes and French. Everybody is the whole scene -- (unintelligible).

Same way here. I mean you were speaking about, if you go back in the background, the heritage, well, it's actually no particular one, but somehow or other it's -- whatever they play is part of going back to the Africans. It got to be some of it.

Well, you know, it's really -- it's when they sort of start talking about the African thing that sometimes you wonder whether they -- I mean there are so many -- I mean they talk of the Africa as though all those people there -- sure, they're black, so they're all the same. But they're not.
I mean just as people (unintelligible) as they are in Europe.
I mean that's why, I think, some of these theories about the music, you know, the African thing -- I wonder really how much of that was right there just wasn't so much of that (unintelligible).
You have to take it as these --
